summary: Eric J. Sharpe (1933–2000) was a scholar in religious studies and Indology. He studied at Hartley Victoria College, University of Manchester under S. G. F. Brandon, and Uppsala University. He held posts at Manchester, Lancaster, Uppsala, and the University of Sydney.

Eric M. Greene is a Buddhist studies and sinology scholar who completed his PhD at UC Berkeley under Robert H. Sharf, also studying with Tōru Funayama and others. He was an assistant professor of religious studies at Yale University (attested 2017).

Eric P. Hamp (1920–2019) was a linguist and Indologist who studied at the Tome School, Amherst College, and Harvard University. He held academic posts at the University of Michigan (1950–1953) and the University of Chicago (~1953–1991).
Eric Reinders works in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and sinology. He studied under mentors Allan G. Grapard and William F. Powell.

Eric Stephen Goodell is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned MA degrees from the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies and the University of Virginia, where he studied under doctoral supervisor Paul Groner.

Erich Frauwallner (1898–1974) was an Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy scholar who completed his doctoral thesis at the University of Vienna. He held multiple positions at the University of Vienna between 1928 and 1964.

Erich Haenisch (1880–1966) was a scholar in sinology, Tibetology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Berlin under Wilhelm Grube, and held professorships at the universities of Göttingen, Leipzig, Berlin, and Munich.

Erich Heintel (1912–2000) was a philosopher who completed his doctorate and habilitation at the University of Vienna. He served as professor of philosophy at the University of Vienna from 1952 to 1982.

Erich Rudolf Jaensch (1883–1940) was a philosopher who studied at Breslau, Göttingen (PhD), and Strasbourg. He held posts at the University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1910–1913) and as ordentlicher Professor at the University of Marburg beginning in 1913.

Erich Schmidt (1853–1913) was a scholar in linguistics and other fields. He studied at Graz, Jena, and Strasbourg under Wilhelm Scherer, and held posts at the universities of Würzburg, Vienna, and Berlin.

Erik Braun is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar. He studied at Harvard University under Janet Gyatso, Saw Tun, John Okell, and Jonathan Evans, and held a post at Harvard University (attested 2010).

Erik Erikson (1902–1994) studied at the University of Oxford. During his career, he held academic posts at the University of California, Berkeley (~1939–1950), the University of Pittsburgh (~1951–1960), and Harvard University (~1960–1970).

Erik Haarh (1929–1993) was a Tibetologist and linguist who studied at the University of Copenhagen. He worked at the Royal Danish Library (1956–1962), Copenhagen (1955), and Aarhus University as department head (1969) and theology professor (1983–1993).

Erik J. Hammerstrom is a scholar in Buddhist studies and sinology. He earned his PhD at Indiana University and served as an assistant professor of religion at Pacific Lutheran University (attested 2016).
Erik Pema Kunsang (b. 1933) is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies figure. He served as director at Rangjung Yeshe Publications (~1981) and as resident teacher at Rangjung Yeshe Gomde Denmark (~1988).

Erik Zürcher (1928–2008) was a sinologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He earned his PhD at Leiden University, studying under Paul Demiéville, Jan Duyvendak, and others. He later served as director at Leiden University (1961–1993).

Erik-Jan Zürcher (b. 1953) is a historian who earned his BA and PhD from Leiden University. He held positions at Radboud University Nijmegen, the University of Amsterdam, the International Institute of Social History, and Leiden University.

Erling von Mende (b. 1940) is a sinologist who studied at Hamburg, Freiburg, Bonn, and Cologne (PhD and Habilitation). He served as professor of sinology at the Free University of Berlin from 1983 to 2007.
Ernest Arthur Gardner (1862–1939) was an archaeologist and historian. He studied at Gonville and Caius College (~1880–1884) and held a post at the University of London (1924–1926).

Ernest Bender (1919–1996) was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at Temple University and the University of Pennsylvania under W. Norman Brown, Zellig Harris, and Henry M. Hoenigswald, later serving as professor at Pennsylvania from 1958 to 1989.
